Revisions to Fiscal 924: Cash in School Buildings
plain_text:
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
POLICY COMMITTEE  
 
October 21, 2026 5:30 p.m. Or Immediately following  
 
1. Chair Want called the meeting to order at 6:07 p.m. 
 
2. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
Present: Committee Members Want, O’Neil-Wong, Taylor, St. John and Student Members 
Mohamed and Langlois. 
   
3. Public Forum 
 
There were no individuals wishing to speak during public forum. 
 
 
6. Approval of the Minutes from the September 16, 2026 Policy Committee meeting. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, duly seconded by Committee Member Taylor, it was 
moved to approve the minutes of the September 16, 2026 Policy Committee.  All were in favor and the 
motion passed. 
 
7. Presentations 
 
There were no presentations. 
 
8. Parent Group Approval under policy Agency and Foundations (CAF) 215:    
Advertising and Use of the District’s Name, Logo and Likeness for fundraising,  
promotions and other related reasons as defined in the policy – by Kelly Jobel,  
Data/Technology, and Matt Upton, Esq., Executive Director of Legal and Policy 
 
Executive Director of Legal and Policy Matt Upton presented a request to recognize Bring It as an 
approved organization authorized to use the District's name, logo, and likeness. He explained that the 
District currently has 15 recognized organizations and that the approval process helps ensure that 
organizations using the District's identity align with its community values.
October 21, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 2 of 5 
 
 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee members discussed whether approval of these organizations should continue to come 
before the Board or be handled administratively. Attorney Upton explained that a policy revision 
would be necessary to delegate that authority to the Administration.  
2. Committee Member Taylor expressed support for retaining Board oversight, noting that the 
number of requests may decrease once the initial registration process is completed.  
3. The Committee generally agreed that the elected Board should maintain responsibility for these 
approvals. 
4. Committee Member Stewart requested additional information regarding Bring It. The Committee 
discussed the organization's longstanding involvement with Manchester students, including after-
school programming at Hillside Middle School, academic support, dance, and enrichment 
opportunities. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, duly seconded by Committee Member Taylor, it was 
moved to approve the proposed addition of Bring IT to the approved group list for the use of the name, 
logo and likeness of the district, under the provisions of policy CAF 215, and forward this item to the 
full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
 
9. Proposed revisions to policy Fiscal 924: Cash in School Buildings – by Kelly    
Jobel, Data/Technology, and Matt Upton, Esq., Executive Director of Legal  
and Policy 
 
Attorney Upton presented proposed revisions to Policy Fiscal 924, Cash in School Buildings. He 
explained that the amendments would clarify the language regarding bank deposits to allow schools to 
make deposits during regular business hours, rather than implying that deposits could only occur after 
hours. 
On motion of Committee Member St. John, duly seconded by Committee Member Taylor, it was moved 
to approve the proposed revisions to Fiscal 924: Cash in School Buildings, and forward this item to the 
full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed.
October 21, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 3 of 5 
 
 
 
 
10. Discussion on policy Students 536: Fund-Raising Activities and possible     
revisions – by Nate Baldwin, Friends of Central Soccer President 
 
The Committee discussed proposed revisions to the District's fundraising policy following concerns and 
recommendations submitted by Nate Baldwin, President of Friends of Central Soccer. 
The Committee Chair explained that preliminary discussions had taken place with Mr. Baldwin, Kelly 
Chobell, and the Board Clerk. Attorney Upton subsequently prepared a revised draft incorporating 
additional changes. Due to an oversight, the draft had not been forwarded to the Clerk for inclusion in 
the original agenda materials. The item was therefore presented for discussion only, with formal 
consideration anticipated at the next Committee meeting. 
Attorney Upton provided background on the existing policy, explaining that it was originally developed 
to address concerns regarding student fundraising, including student incentives, accountability, and 
appropriate use of funds. However, the current policy does not adequately address more complex 
fundraising activities undertaken by independent community organizations. 
The proposed revisions would provide greater flexibility for community organizations seeking to 
support District programs, including provisions for multiyear fundraising initiatives, memorandums of 
understanding, and clearly defined fundraising purposes. Attorney Upton also emphasized the 
importance of maintaining records of authorized fundraising activities to protect the community from 
potentially fraudulent solicitations. 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Taylor asked whether the delay in revising the policy would create 
difficulties for Friends of Central Soccer or other organizations. Attorney Upton indicated that he 
did not anticipate any immediate issues, as the Administration remains in communication with 
the organizations. 
2. Committee Member Stewart expressed support for the proposed revisions, noting that the 
changes would encourage community partnerships and provide additional opportunities for 
organizations to support District programs and students. 
3. The Committee expressed appreciation to Mr. Baldwin for bringing forward his concerns and 
recommendations.
October 21, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 4 of 5 
 
 
 
No action was taken. The proposed revisions will return to the Committee for consideration at its next 
meeting. 
  
11. Minimum Wage – at the 9/14/2026 BOSC Meeting, Vice Chair O’Connell    
Requested that the Policy Committee review the district’s minimum wage policy 
 
The Committee discussed a request from Vice Chair O'Connell to review the District's minimum wage. 
The Board Clerk explained that the District does not currently have a formal minimum wage policy. 
Rather, the Board approved an increase to a minimum wage of $15 per hour on August 22, 2022, 
following a financial impact analysis conducted by the Finance Department. The fiscal impact at that 
time was approximately $810,000. 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member St. John expressed support for establishing a formal minimum wage policy, 
increasing the District's minimum wage to $25 per hour, and incorporating an annual cost-of-
living adjustment tied to inflation. 
2. Committee members discussed the financial implications of such an increase and the possibility 
of implementing incremental wage adjustments over multiple years. Committee Member Taylor 
suggested that the Administration evaluate several options for reaching the proposed $25 
minimum wage, considering the District's current fiscal challenges. 
On motion by Committee Member St. John, duly seconded by Committee Member Taylor, with a 
friendly amendment incorporated, to forward the matter to the Administration for review and 
preparation of a fiscal impact analysis regarding establishing a $25 per hour minimum wage, including 
options for incremental increases over multiple years and an annual cost-of-living adjustment tied to 
inflation, with the findings to be forwarded to the Committee on Finance and Facilities for further 
consideration.  All were in favor and the motion passed.
October 21, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 5 of 5 
 
 
 
12. TABLED ITEMS 
 
There were no tabled items this evening. 
 
13.   NEW BUSINESS 
 
There was no new business presented. 
 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
14. If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn.  
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, duly seconded by Committee Member St. John, it was 
moved to adjourn.  All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 6:32 p.m. 
 
True Copy.  Attest. 
Respectfully Submitted, 
  
 
Clerk of Committee
